draft.title: Activity analysis
card: An activity analysis is a close look at a sport or activity to find what it demands from the body. Coaches do it before they plan training.
It records the movement skills used, such as jumping, kicking or changing direction. It also records the muscles that do most of the work.
It finds which energy systems supply most of the energy, and which fitness components matter most, such as speed, endurance or flexibility.
The results let the coach match training to the activity. Training then builds what the athlete actually needs in competition.
draft.remember: Analyse the activity first, then build training to match what it demands.

a.q: Why does a coach do an activity analysis before writing a training program?
opts: To match training to what the activity demands
To measure how fit each athlete is at present
To choose which athletes make the final team
To check that the athletes have given consent
a.why: An activity analysis studies the activity itself, so training can match its skills, energy systems, muscles and fitness components. Measuring each athlete's fitness is a different task, because the analysis looks at the activity and not at the athlete.
a.clue: The analysis looks at the activity, not the athlete.

b.q: Jess coaches a 100 m sprint squad. Her analysis finds the race lasts about 11 seconds and needs a very fast, powerful start. What should she do with this finding?
opts: Plan training that builds speed and explosive power
Plan long, steady runs to build general endurance
Plan training that builds mainly flexibility
Plan training based on what the squad prefers
b.why: A very short, fast effort with a powerful start calls for speed and power training. Long steady runs are tempting, but they do not match the demands of an 11 second race.
b.clue: Match training to a short, fast, powerful effort.
